input.quote: Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service.
input.rationale: Preferred position met: Section 24.1 lets us assign to Affiliates and successors without consent, Section 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment (consent not unreasonably withheld, never to a Customer competitor), and Section 24.4 removes any Vendor right arising on our change of control. Section 13.3 confirms licence transferability.

input.quote: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.1 correctly leaves Customer Data and our pre-existing IP with us, but Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of Deliverables built specifically for us with only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence back — below the fallback (which requires at least a perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable licence) and in tension with Section 13.2. We reversed the assignment and added a perpetual licence fallback; Vendor Technology stays with Vendor under Section 14.3.

input.quote: Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer.
input.rationale: Sections 13.1–13.3 meet the preferred position: Affiliates and contractors are covered, paid-up/embedded software is licensed perpetually and irrevocably, revocation is limited to material uncured breach after notice and cure, and rights are transferable to an Affiliate or successor. The narrower Deliverable licence in Section 14.2 is addressed under the IP rule rather than flagged twice here.
